videos.title: One habit that survives a bad week
videos.description: Tiny, obvious, and tied to an existing cue — so it still happens when motivation is gone.

notes.abstract: Habits fail when they depend on motivation; they stick when they are tiny and cued.
points: Attach the habit to something you already do daily.
Make the first version embarrassingly small.
Track streaks lightly, not as punishment.
notes.conclusion: If you only do the habit on good days, it is still a mood — shrink it until bad days count.

videos.title: Focus blocks without drama
videos.description: 25–50 minute blocks, one target, and a shutdown ritual that actually closes the loop.

notes.abstract: Focus is a protected block with one outcome, not a vibe of “being busy.”
points: Name the single deliverable before you start.
Silence inputs for the block length you chose.
End with a one-line note on what remains.
notes.conclusion: Open loops kill the next block — write the residue down before you context-switch.

videos.title: Weekly review in 20 minutes
videos.description: A lightweight review: wins, leaks, and one adjustment — not a second job.

notes.abstract: Weekly reviews work when they are short enough to repeat.
points: List wins so your brain sees progress.
Choose a single adjustment for next week.
notes.conclusion: A perfect review you skip is useless — keep it under 20 minutes.

videos.title: Asking for feedback you can use
videos.description: Specific questions beat “any thoughts?” — and you decide what to adopt.

notes.abstract: Useful feedback is solicited with a sharp question and filtered by your goals.
points: Ask about one moment or artifact, not your whole self.
Adopt what matches your aim; discard the rest politely.
notes.conclusion: Unscoped feedback becomes noise — narrow the ask.

videos.title: Decisions with a default and a deadline
videos.description: Stop re-opening choices: set a default, a timebox, and a revisit rule.

notes.abstract: Indecision is often missing defaults and deadlines, not missing information.
points: Write the default if you do nothing.
Define when you are allowed to revisit.
notes.conclusion: Revisiting without new information is rumination — close the loop.

resorts.name: Weekly review template
resorts.summary: A one-page weekly review you can copy into any notes app.
resorts.intro:
Sections:

1. Wins (3 bullets)
2. Energy (what drained / what restored)
3. One leak
4. Next week’s single focus

Keep it short enough that Sunday-you still does it.

resorts.name: Small reading stack
resorts.summary: Three practical books worth finishing over collecting.
resorts.intro:
Prefer finishing one practical book over collecting ten.

Suggested stance: take notes as actions, not quotes.

If a chapter does not change a next action, skim faster.
